Show HN: Parents Inbox – Communication Guide for Schools

At a dinner party with other parents recently, the conversation turned to the challenges we all have with communication coming from our children's schools. Emails and Texts and App notifications, coming from Teachers, Admins, PTA, After-Care programs. Overlapping information, buried key details, verbose fluff. An avalanche of text every day that must be carefully parsed to find important info.

This seems to be a universal problem and certainly one I experience every day. So literally before dinner was over I built the first version of this site on my phone with Claude.

I think the main problem is that the folks who are responsible for communication just don't have the tools and experience to know what good communication really looks like, or the parents perspective hasn't been demonstrated to them to give them more empathy. So I am hoping this can help. Feel free to share if you have the same problem with your school.

Show HN: Risphai – picks the AI model, tools and prompt for each request

I noticed that a lot of non-technical people don’t use AI to its full extent. Like they use the wrong model for the task, the wrong reasoning effort, or vague prompts. That gap between "what the AI can do" and "what people actually get" is what I wanted to fix.

So I spent the last two years in my spare time building a consumer AI product that tries to fix this issue.

This is how it works:
When it receives the request, an LLM decides the task type (chat, reasoning, coding, writing) and the tool calls that are needed (web search, image generation, video generation, audio generation). Then it routes it to a suitable model and applies a prompt based on the task type. If it's a media generation task, it rewrites the prompt into a detailed one using prompt formulas (the prompt formulas for specific styles are mentioned in the system prompt). The LLM that is used for answering the request can also use a map, generate a mermaid diagram, generate a quiz or flashcards, generate files, etc.

A limitation right now is that routing adds latency, but I'm currently experimenting with decision-models like Jev, PPLX Decider, etc. and might use decision-models to route to the right LLM and give the tool calls like web search and media generation to the answering LLM.

It launched this week, so it's still early and I will keep improving it and adding new things.

Also sign-up/in is required to prevent abuse.

I’d really like honest feedback: what’s confusing, what’s missing, etc.

Show HN: I turned my kids' old Yoto Player into an Audiobookshelf player

My kids love their Yotos and I love Audiobookshelf. I wanted something in between that works as they get older and more control. I had two old Gen 2 players lying around that Yoto no longer supports.

It turns the player into an Audiobookshelf client. You browse your library with the two knobs, the 16x16 screen shows tiny cover art, and favourites and downloads sync back to the server. Its still keeps the NFC card concept, but they're optional: you can link books/favourites to any NFC card. It all runs locally, with no Yoto account or cloud.

It does require opening the player and soldering some wires to flash the initial firmware, but then its OTA after that.

Disclaimer: Its all Claude Code, Its an idea I've been slowly tinkering around in my spare time and never got very far so. I threw Claude Code at it and I was amazed at how well it did. Flashing, reading logs and fixing things - leaving me to just perform physical button presses and checks.

AI as a part of capitalism – the right way to go

The way things go now are obsiously flawed.

1. AI companies objective is to get rid of a very large part of jobs, thus converting a large part of consumers into jobless people - who are very bad at consuming.

2. They also take other people's and companie's content for free, turning them into own profits, thus removing any incentives to create such content in the future.

Proposed solution.

1. All data models are created anew.

2. All of the model content should be marked and paid for to its creators in a proportional amount to each specific training data usage.

3. No payment = no use in the model, unless a creator provides a free license to LLM's.

4. Any commercial data needs an explicit permission to be used in training.

5. Profits made on data with no explicit owner (say, Shakespeare) are to be paid off to the respective country.

6. This policy is enforced worldwide.

When implemented, this policy will ensure that:

a. Many people whose jobs suffer remain part of the AI economy or can become parts of it;

b. Open-source software, photographers, artists, etc. will receive their rightful share of AI profits;

c. People will have a very good incentive to keep on creating.

Show HN: Fakeipedia – Wikipedia for worlds that don't exist

Hi HN!

Fakeipedia is an automatic world-building platform which takes an imagined world and makes a whole wiki that you can endlessly explore by clicking red links.

I came up with this idea a few months ago after playing around with worldbuilding in Gemini, but I didn't want to release it until a powerful enough model could do it justice, and I decided that Argon is creative enough to write articles that are worth reading. I was surprised how well it turned out and how engaging some of the writing actually is.

If you want to generate an article there is a nominal charge attached ($0.90), which helps cover AI/Stripe costs, and I think I just about break even. You can also steer the generation ala choose-your-own-adventure books when generating a new article. Everything generated is free and public for everyone to see.

I hope you like it and I'm very much open to hearing about new world ideas/features that would make this project better.

Show HN: Donut Browser, the most private anti-detect browser

Hi everyone!

About 2 years ago, I began to work on Donut Browser as a tool to manage browser profiles, which over time has evolved into a proper anti-detect browser.

Anti-detect browsers let you create browser profiles that look like as if you have a completely different computer. I believe Donut is the most private anti-detect browser because:
- It has no telemetry and doesn't track your browsing activity
- It spoofs your browser identity in a way that looks like a real device for every profile
- It notifies you when a website takes a snapshot of your browser identity
- It is built on top of Chromium and lets you block ads and trackers at the DNS level without relying on Manifest V2
- It lets you create unlimited profiles (the first anti-detect browser to do that)
- It supports Linux, which not all anti-detect browsers do!

I use Donut as my main browser and the only other browser I have installed is Tor. If you are into privacy, it offers a lot better experience than Firefox containers or writing your own scripts to manage profiles!

If anyone is going to try it, would love to hear any feedback!

Poll: Stanford students preferred 22% less salary for annual equity liquidity

I’m one of the founders of Street. We ran a poll with 500+ people in our Stanford network about how they’d choose between two startup offers.
Both had the same role, vesting and $1m equity grant. One paid $180k, with the equity locked until an IPO or acquisition. The other paid $140k, but allowed them to sell up to 5% of their shares each year.
More than half picked the $140k offer.
We work on shareholder liquidity at private companies, which is why we wanted to look into this. These were hypothetical offers, but I thought the result was worth sharing here. Happy to answer questions about the poll.

Show HN: Relay – A Mac app that adds /relay command to Claude, Codex and Cursor

Simply put, Relay is just a copy-paster between Claude, Codex and Cursor. It adds a /relay command to those GUIs that just sends the chat history since last over to the other side.

I’ve been working on this small Mac app called Kanary that offers essential features. While building it, I found myself stupidly repeating the process of being a messenger between Claude and Codex.

Then I thought, why not build a feature that helps my development process? What if Kanary could be a meta-app that bridges between harnesses? That’s when I hit on the idea of a meta harness. A wrapper that works IN the GUI apps that we already use, not a new app.

It’s still just a copy-paster, but it has changed how I work tremendously. So far it’s a painkiller for me, not a vitamin. I’d love to hear what you think of this simple tool that does this one simple thing.

75 free relays per week. Copy is always free.

Emu Concept – Make AI Follows Your Rules. (Feedback Wanted)

If I give these agents access to tools/connectors/data they just "assume" what I want or what it should do rather than asking me? And even if I set these for a specific agent then what happens when a newer personal agent comes out? Do I have to reconfigure again my rules for each flavor of personal agents or harness?

This is where our initial idea stems from and we need feedback:

Emu is a self-learning on-device AI guardian that makes AI agents follow your rules. Also the video above kind of just highlights Emu's concept thought process.
